newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ powerbroker says he could jump either way.
newsitem.headline: NZ powerbroker says he could jump either way.

text.p: The leader of the nationalist New Zealand First party said on Tuesday he would negotiate with the outgoing conservative government and the Labour Party to form a new government after inconclusive elections.
Populist leader Winston Peters said he could go either way, and it would not necessarily be harmful if talks dragged on until Christmas.
"It's better to take time to get it right," he said.
Peters agreed with a remark by caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger that the chances of his conservative National Party staying in office were about even.
"I think if that's 50-50 Labour, 50-50 National, that's about even, yes, that's fair enough," Peters said.

He was giving his first detailed comments since election night on Saturday. New Zealand First's 17 seats gave it the balance of power between National and its allies, with 53 seats, and Labour and the left-wing Alliance, with 50.

Both National and Labour have said they aim to form a government with the support of New Zealand First, which campaigned on pledges to put ordinary people's interests over those of foreign investors and big business.
Peters also weighed in with criticism of the central bank's zero to two percent inflation target, and said the New Zealand dollar was clearly too high for the country's exporters.
His comments at a news conference pushed the kiwi dollar downwards, but international credit rating agency Standard and Poors gave a reassuring commentary on the election outcome.
S&P affirmed New Zealand's ratings and said it did not expect the inconclusive election result to lead to economic policy changes that would affect the ratings.
